skill.name: skill-share
skill.description: Guides AI agents through creating, validating, packaging, and sharing reusable skills with a team through Slack and Rube.
skill.summary: Create structured AI skills and share reviewed packages with a team.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The external-command alert is a false positive because SKILL.md lines 59-66 contain a Markdown example, not executable Ruby or shell syntax. The workflow has a separate medium-risk behavior because it can automatically send skill metadata and direct links to Slack without requiring final user confirmation.

remediation.issue: The workflow can publish skill metadata and direct links to Slack automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Require a preview and explicit user confirmation before posting, and display the selected workspace, channel, message, and links.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md lines 59-66 contain a Markdown fenced example describing expected workflow steps. The backticks are delimiters only, with no Ruby interpolation, shell command, or executable code.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Slack Publication Without Final Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow automatically posts skill metadata and direct links to Slack, but it does not require a final review or confirmation before transmission. This can expose internal names, descriptions, or file links to an unintended channel.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly states that skill information and direct links are sent automatically. No confirmation or message preview step is defined before posting.

content.value_statement: Teams often create reusable AI skills without a consistent structure or discovery process. This skill guides creation, validation, packaging, and Slack sharing through Rube.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of hyphen-named skill directories with SKILL.md metadata.
Recommends standard scripts, references, and assets directories for organized skill packages.
Checks required metadata, naming conventions, and structure before packaging.
Directs a compatible agent to create a distributable zip archive.
Uses Rube Slack operations to find channels and share skill metadata or links.
limitations: The package contains workflow guidance but no bundled creation, validation, or packaging scripts.
File creation and archive generation require a compatible agent with filesystem access.
Slack sharing requires a configured Rube connection, channel access, and posting permission.
The documented validation process does not define a formal schema or automated test suite.

use_cases.title: Standardize Internal Skills
use_cases.description: Create reusable team skills with consistent directories, metadata, and packaging conventions.

use_cases.title: Announce New Team Tools
use_cases.description: Prepare a skill summary and share the reviewed package in a designated Slack channel.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Submissions
use_cases.description: Check naming, metadata, directory structure, and packaging readiness before internal distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill named [skill-name] that helps with [task]. Include clear metadata, instructions, and a standard directory structure.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a simple reusable skill from a short requirement.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the skill at [path]. Check its name, SKILL.md metadata, directory structure, instructions, and packaging readiness. Report required corrections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess a skill before sharing it with a team.

prompt_templates.title: Package and Preview a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate and package the skill at [path]. Prepare a Slack announcement preview with its name, summary, archive location, and intended channel.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a distribution package without posting it automatically.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Governed Sharing Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create and validate a skill for [workflow]. Package it, find approved Slack channels through Rube, and request confirmation before sending any message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an advanced workflow with explicit review and publishing controls.

output_examples.input: Create a skill named release-notes-reviewer for checking product release notes.
output: Created a release-notes-reviewer skill directory with SKILL.md.
Added organized locations for scripts, references, and assets.
Prepared the skill for validation and packaging.

output_examples.input: Validate the customer-support-summary skill before distribution.
output: The skill name follows the required hyphenated format.
The metadata contains a name and description.
The instructions need a clearer activation condition before packaging.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Slack announcement for the approved dependency-audit skill.
output_examples.output: Preview prepared for the selected engineering channel. It includes the skill name, summary, package location, and a confirmation request before posting.

best_practices: Review generated instructions and metadata before validation and packaging.
Preview the Slack message, destination channel, and shared links before confirming publication.
Keep sensitive data, credentials, and private references outside distributed skill packages.
anti_patterns: Do not publish automatically when the destination channel or audience is unclear.
Do not treat directory presence as proof that scripts or references are complete.
Do not include credentials, private tokens, or confidential content in skill metadata.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It guides an AI agent to create a structured skill directory, metadata, supporting folders, validation results, and a distributable package.

faq.question: Does it include executable creation scripts?
faq.answer: No. The current package contains instructions only and depends on the agent and available tools for implementation.

faq.question: Can it share a skill through Slack?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes Rube operations for finding channels and posting skill metadata, summaries, and links.

faq.question: What is required for Slack sharing?
faq.answer: A configured Rube connection, permission to access the workspace, and permission to post in the selected channel are required.

faq.question: Does it validate every skill requirement?
faq.answer: No. It checks documented structure and metadata conventions, but it does not provide a formal schema or automated validation suite.

faq.question: How should teams prevent unintended sharing?
faq.answer: Require a message preview and explicit confirmation after showing the workspace, channel, message content, package location, and shared links.
